page.layout: One printed page, the left one of the scan. Top: an ornamental rule. Then a centred title, "STATUS CONTROVERSIÆ IN GENERE.", and below it a paragraph with a large initial P, set in display type. Then a rule, a centred heading "Contra MERITVM DE CONGRVO.", and "CAP. I." Below that, a paragraph with a woodcut initial M, and a marginal note in the right margin. Running head: none. Catchword at the right below the last line. Right half of the scan: blank, with show-through only.

main_text.head: STATUS CONTROVERSIÆ IN GENERE.
main_text.p: PRotestantes OPERA BO-NA ad salutem necessaria esse, & destinata media defendunt.

p.i: Pontificii Doctores EA præterea PROPRIE DICTA MERITA esse venditant.

main_text.p: MERITVM vero duplex esse statuunt, 1. De Congruo. 2. De Condigno.
main_text.head: Contra MERITVM DE CONGRVO.
CAP. I.
main_text.p: Meritum de Congruo ( definitore {a}Vega ) est Actio libera, cui congruum sit, ut par aliquod respondeat Præmium. Opiniones Eorum, de hoc Merito, ad Quæstiones tres reduci possunt.Vega, lib. 8. de Justif. cap. 8.

page.notes: The right half of the scan is blank apart from show-through of the reverse page, which is not transcribed. A faint small mark at the top right and a light stain at the bottom right are not printed text. The catchword "A Quæst." stands at the line end, not below it; it is transcribed as the catchword. The reference mark "a" is an italic letter in the text and in the margin. The note "Justif." may be "Iustif." in the original, but the scan gives "Justif." as printed. The notes are small, so the abbreviations "lib." and "cap." are read with some uncertainty.
